summary: Batakrishna Ghosh (1905–1950) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel around 1930–1935. He served as Librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Beata Grant (born 1954) is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Stanford University (c. 1981–1987) and was appointed Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis around 1989.

Beatrice Erskine Lane (1878–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, earned an MA from Columbia University, and became a professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer (1941–2011) was an Indologist who earned her Magister and Dr. phil. at the University of Heidelberg. She held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Maryland, College Park, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Bedřich Hrozný (1879–1952) was a linguist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (c. 1905–1919) and the University of Prague (c. 1919–1952).
Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who founded Bukkyo Seito Doshikai. He studied at Toyo University around 1896–1900 and later held a post there.
Bemé Shyi Drol studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who completed his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein in 2001. By 2008, he served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado under the doctoral supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London. She held positions at the University of Virginia and became Lecturer in East Asian Religions at the University of Bristol around 2017.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who earned an MA from the University of Calcutta and a D.Litt. from the University of London. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Calcutta from 1913 to 1948.

Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a Sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held professorships at the University of California, Los Angeles, and Princeton University.

Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and studied with Janet Gyatso and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. Around 2010–2016, he served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan.
Benjamin Fleming is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

Benjamin Lewis Rice (1837–1927) worked in Indology and archaeology. He served as Director of Public Instruction in Mysore and Coorg (c. 1868–1883) and as Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (c. 1884–1889).
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Yale University (c. 1985–1989) and Harvard University (c. 1991–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan around 2003.

Benjamin Wood is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Toronto under the supervision of Frances Garrett. He also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo in 1915. He served as president of Taisho University and Tokai Gakuen Women's College, and led the Sanko Research Institute and Sanko Library.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Calcutta and Dhaka universities under Alfred Foucher and Haraprasad Shastri. He directed the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and served at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
